text: Git branching is an important skill in any version control workflow. A branch lets you work on new code without affecting the main project. Developers often create feature branches to build and test a single feature safely. When the work is finished, you merge the branch back into the main line. On team projects, you usually open a pull request before merging, so others can review your changes and discuss improvements. This process keeps the code organised and reduces mistakes. By using branches, merging, and pull requests together, teams can work faster and more confidently, even when several people change the same project at once.
